p: Uz: That is, of the country of Idumea, La 4:21, or bordering on it: for the land was called by the name of Uz, the son of Dishan, the son of Seir Ge 36:28.
upright: Since he was a Gentile and not a Jew and yet is pronounced upright and without hypocrisy, it declares that among the heathen God revealed himself.
one that feared God: By this it is declared what is meant by an upright and just man.
substance also was seven thousand sheep: His children and riches are declared, to commend his virtue in his prosperity and his patience and constancy when God took them from him.
the east: Meaning, the Arabians, Chaldeans, Idumeans etc.
sanctified them: That is, commanded them to be sanctified: meaning, that they should consider the faults that they had committed, and reconcile themselves for the same.

offered burnt offerings according to the: That is, he offered for each of his children an offering of reconciliation, which declared his religion toward God, and the care that he had for his children.
cursed God in their hearts: In Hebrew it is, "blessed God", which is sometimes taken for blaspheming and cursing, as it is here and in 1Ki 21:10,13.
continually: While the feast lasted.
sons of God came to present: Meaning the angels, who are called the sons of God because they are willing to execute his will.
before the LORD: Because our infirmity cannot comprehend God in his majesty, he is set forth to us as a King, that our capacity may be able to understand that which is spoken of him.
came also among them: This declares that although Satan is an adversary to God, yet he is compelled to obey him, and do him all homage, without whose permission and appointment he can do nothing.
comest thou: This question is asked for our infirmity: for God knew where he had come from.
From going to and fro in: In this is described the nature of Satan, which is always seeking his prey, 1Pe 5:8.
nought: He fears you not for your own sake, but for the blessing that he received from you.
an hedge about him: Meaning, the grace of God, which served Job as a rampart against all temptations.
touch all that he hath: This signifies that Satan is not able to touch us, but it is God that must do it.

thy face: Satan notes the vice to which men are commonly subjected, that is, to hide their rebellion and to be content with God in the time of prosperity which view is disclosed in the time of their adversity.
thy power: God does not give Satan power over man to gratify him, but to declare that he has no power over man, but that which God gives him.
presence of the LORD: That is, went to execute that which God had permitted him to do for else he can never go out of God's presence.
Sabeans fell upon them: That is, the Arabians.
fire of God is fallen from: Which was also done by the craft of Satan, to tempt Job even more grievously, so he might see that not only men were his enemies, but that God made war against him.
sons and thy daughters were eating: This last plague declares that when one plague is past which seems hard to bear, God can send us another far more grievous, to try his and teach them obedience.

rent his mantle: Which came not from impatience, but declares that the children of God are not insensible like blocks, but that in their patience they feel affliction and grief of mind: yet they do not rebel against God as the wicked do.
thither: That is, into the belly of the earth, which is the mother of all.
blessed be the name of the: By this he confesses that God is just and good, although his hand is sore on him.
foolishly: But declared that God did all things according to justice and equity.
